value: Smoking group-specific MVPA accuracy was positively related to attentional bias in the right postcentral gyrus, whereas more negative relationships were detected in the rostral anterior cingulate cortex, left inferior frontal gyrus, and left cerebellum.
The rostral anterior cingulate cortex/ventromedial prefrontal cortex findings may reflect conditioned associations and the regulation of conditioned responses to emotionally salient drug cues.
These findings indicate smoking-related effects on the neural correlates of attentional bias, possibly reflecting conditioned drug effects or maladaptive neural processes among active smokers.
